title: RandomNumberGenerator seeding produces correlated streams when instances are created in quick succession
body:
> [!INFO]
> **AI disclosure**: I investigated the bug and wrote the failing reproduction myself. AI assistance was used for searching prior issues, light editing, and reorganising this description for clarity. The diagnosis and reproduction are mine.

### Tested versions

Reproduced on Godot 4.6.2 stable. Same code path is unchanged on `master`.

### What's wrong

`RandomPCG::randomize()` in `core/math/random_pcg.cpp:42-44` derives the seed from a microsecond-resolution clock value:

```cpp
seed(((uint64_t)OS::get_singleton()->get_unix_time() + OS::get_singleton()->get_ticks_usec()) * pcg.state + PCG_DEFAULT_INC_64);
```

The `(uint64_t)` cast on `get_unix_time()` truncates to whole seconds, leaving `ticks_usec` as the only sub-second contributor. Constructing a `RandomNumberGenerator` completes in well under a microsecond on modern hardware, so consecutive `RandomNumberGenerator.new()` calls in the same frame routinely read the same timestamp, get the same seed, and emit byte-identical streams.

Since #66989 (Godot 4.0 beta) the constructor auto-calls `randomize()`, so the defect now reaches every default-constructed instance, including code as ordinary as a per-roll RNG.

### Reproduction

Drop on a `Node` in any Godot 4 project:

```gdscript
extends Node

const TRIALS := 5000
const DICE := 5

func _ready() -> void:
    var rolls: Array[PackedInt32Array] = []
    for t in TRIALS:
        var rng := RandomNumberGenerator.new()
        var r := PackedInt32Array(); r.resize(DICE)
        for d in DICE: r[d] = rng.randi_range(1, 6)
        rolls.append(r)
    var ties := 0
    for t in range(1, TRIALS):
        if rolls[t] == rolls[t - 1]: ties += 1
    print("ties: %d (expected ~%.2f)" % [ties, float(TRIALS - 1) / pow(6.0, DICE)])
    get_tree().quit()
```

Expected for a fair RNG: roughly 0.64 ties.

### Empirical results

| Run                                                                             | Identical consecutive 5d6 | Expected |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------: | -------: |
| Godot 4.6.2 stable, headless, M-series Mac, N=5000                              | 2168                      | 0.64     |
| Godot 4.6.2 stable, headless, fast Windows desktop release build, N=100,000,000 | 57,287,074                | ~12,860  |
| Pure C++ reproduction (no GDScript overhead), N=5000                            | 4784                      | 0.64     |

Magnitude depends on per-iteration time relative to one microsecond, which is the resolution of the entropy source. Faster builds and faster hardware make the bug more visible; slower configurations can hide it.

### Why this is filed despite #48087

Same bug was reported in #48087 (April 2021, Godot 3.3) under "randomize() often producing same seed when called in `_ready()`". The reporter quoted the same line of `random_pcg.cpp` and proposed a fix. The change that landed added `unix_time` to the formula, but the cast truncates fractional seconds, so calls within the same wall-clock second still collapse to identical seeds. The original failure mode was not addressed.

#66989 (Oct 2022) made the constructor auto-randomize, broadening the user-visible impact of the still-unfixed seeding bug from "explicit `randomize()` callers" to "every `RandomNumberGenerator.new()`".

### Expected behavior

Two `RandomNumberGenerator` instances created in succession with no explicit seed should be statistically independent, matching what the class reference describes ("multiple instances, each with their own seed and state").

### Reproduction project and prior reports

- Self-contained reproduction: <https://github.com/atelico/better-godot-rng/tree/main/tests/rng_experiment>
- Prior reports: #48087 (closed), #66989 (related, broadened impact), #27171 (downstream PCG seeding fix, unrelated to entropy source).
